title: Music and Lusotropicalism in Late Colonial Luanda | BUALA
text: September 1, 2010 - Singing in local languages created a new and different sound. Musicians drew upon a variety of resources in their compositions and performances –fables from different ethnic groups, songs sung in the contexts of wakes and carnival rivalries, Congolese guitar styles, Latin American dance beats, Angolan instruments (like the dikanza and kissange),7 foreign cinema, European and American fashion not to mention their own experiences.8 The implications of this mixing, far from symbolizing a lusotropical creolization, actually stood that notion on its head.
